title: Complaints and what became of them
question: How many ethics matters and whistleblower reports come in each year, and how many end in a penalty or a corrective action?
finding: The Ethics Commission opened 713 enforcement matters in fiscal 2022 to 2026 and issued 52 penalties in the same years, about one penalty for every 14 matters opened. The Controller's whistleblower programme received 817 reports in fiscal 2026; of 422 investigations closed, 115 (27%) led a department or contractor to act. The Commission resolved 23 whistleblower-retaliation matters in fiscal 2025 and imposed no penalty in any of them.
how: Ethics Commission figures are read from its quarterly enforcement reports: for each fiscal year the last report that gives a running count of matters opened ('So far in FY..'), with the count of matters in progress and completed where the report prints them. Penalties are counted from the Commission's penalty file by the fiscal year of the penalty date. The whistleblower columns repeat the Controller's annual figures as tabulated in the site’s “Audits and official documents” page (screen whistleblower-trend), where the dispositions and the departments are set out; the fiscal 2026 and retaliation figures are checked against the reports' text.
limits: A matter opened is not a violation found: most complaints are dismissed because the Commission has no jurisdiction or the facts do not support them, many matters end in a warning letter or advice, and penalties issued in a year mostly close matters opened in earlier years, so the two columns are not the same cases. The running count is 'so far' at the date of the last report of the year, usually in June, so the year's true total is a little higher. Whistleblower reports cover every kind of workplace complaint, not only the five routes on this page. The Commission's investigations are confidential until resolved, so matters in progress cannot be described.
